top_stories.title: Pass the Passkey: A Novel Attack Surface in Passwordless Authentication
top_stories.summary: A novel attack surface in passkey-based passwordless authentication has been identified, centered on relying parties failing to validate the User Verified (UV) flag during authentication. This implementation gap can silently downgrade multi-factor authentication to a single factor, undermining the security guarantees of passkey deployments.

top_stories.title: Windows July 2026 updates bring passkeys, hotpatching, and safer networking
top_stories.summary: Microsoft's July 2026 Windows updates establish passkeys as the default phishing-resistant authentication method in Microsoft Entra ID. The update also introduces free Arc-enabled hotpatching for Windows Server 2025 and improvements to remote desktop networking resilience.

top_stories.title: Suppliers, logins, and AI tools are all becoming attack paths
top_stories.summary: CrowdStrike's 2026 Threat Hunting Report finds cybercriminals and state-backed groups are increasingly abusing trusted identities, cloud services, AI tools, and software supply chains to gain access while evading detection. Intrusion activity grew approximately 4% over the past year, with attackers focusing more on exploiting trusted access paths and legitimate infrastructure.

top_stories.title: Non-human identities are 91% of everything active in production
top_stories.summary: A new report finds that non-human identities (NHIs) account for 91% of all active identities in production environments, with only 20% of non-human activity occurring during standard business hours. The findings highlight the scale of machine credentials—including API keys, service accounts, and pipeline roles—operating in cloud environments like AWS.

top_stories.title: Kali365 Weaponizes Microsoft Authentication Against US Companies: New Enterprise Risk
top_stories.summary: A phishing kit called Kali365 is exploiting Microsoft's device code authentication flow to gain unauthorized access to corporate resources at US organizations. Attackers use attacker-controlled device codes that victims approve on legitimate Microsoft authentication pages, resulting in access and refresh tokens that provide persistent access to email, documents, and cloud resources.

news.title: Cloudflare OS goes open source with a record of everything its agents read
news.summary: Cloudflare open sourced its agent platform, Cloudflare OS, which tracks every resource an AI agent reads and attaches that record to any output the agent produces. When another user opens that output, the platform checks their access permissions against the underlying data source before displaying any content.

news.title: How AI-powered phishing killed blocklists for good
news.summary: Push Security argues that AI-powered phishing attacks generate disposable infrastructure that renders traditional blocklist-based defenses obsolete. The article promotes browser-level, technique-based detection as an alternative approach to identifying phishing attempts that bypass domain and signature-based indicators.

news.title: Leaked n8n API Tokens Exposed Live Instances to Credential Theft
news.summary: GitGuardian researchers discovered 4,576 unique n8n API tokens exposed in public GitHub commits, linked to 1,255 hostnames, with 321 live instances actively accepting the leaked credentials. Researchers demonstrated four attack methods using the exposed tokens to access sensitive data and downstream credentials without exploiting any software vulnerability.

news.title: Device Code Phishing Up 1,500% in 2026; Vishing Doubles
news.summary: Device code phishing attacks have increased 1,500% in 2026, with vishing attacks doubling, as attackers adopt newer social engineering techniques. These methods are specifically designed to bypass entrenched security controls, including MFA, by exploiting the OAuth device authorization flow to steal authentication tokens without requiring credential theft.

news.title: Phishing service spoofs RingCentral to steal Microsoft 365 accounts
news.summary: The Greatness phishing-as-a-service platform has expanded its capabilities to include adversary-in-the-middle attacks and device-code phishing targeting Microsoft 365 accounts, now spoofing RingCentral as a lure. The campaign specifically targets Microsoft 365 credentials and authentication tokens, bypassing MFA protections through session hijacking techniques.

news.title: Varonis Agent IBAC keeps AI agents within their intended boundaries
news.summary: Varonis has introduced Agent IBAC (Intent-Based Access Control), a capability designed to enforce access controls for AI agents by detecting intent drift in real time. The solution addresses the challenge of AI agents requiring broad access while ensuring their actions remain within intended boundaries.

news.title: Greatness PhaaS Adds Device Code Phishing to Bypass MFA and Steal Tokens
news.summary: The Greatness phishing-as-a-service toolkit has added device code phishing capabilities that abuse OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant flows to bypass MFA and steal authentication tokens. The technique uses adversary-in-the-middle methods to capture credentials and session tokens, rendering traditional MFA protections ineffective.

news.title: Keyv-Linked npm Worm Poisons Hundreds of Packages, Plants Claude Code and VS Code Hooks
news.summary: A credential-stealing npm worm originating in keyv@6.0.0 spread to hundreds of packages across the npm registry on August 4, 2026. SafeDep verified 353 poisoned versions across 79 package names, with broader estimates reaching 868 packages affected across multiple organizations.

news.title: Watch out — Microsoft login pages are being abused as hackers try and lure in unlucky victims, here's what to look out for
news.summary: Hackers are abusing Microsoft login pages to gain unauthorized access to corporate accounts across approximately 120 organizations. The attack bypassed MFA entirely and resulted in access to mail, files, Teams, SharePoint, and calendars without stealing passwords.

news.title: Edit on-prem Exchange attributes in Exchange Online with writeback for cloud-managed remote mailboxes
news.summary: Microsoft has made Exchange attribute writeback for cloud-managed remote mailboxes generally available. The feature allows administrators to manage Exchange mailbox attributes in Exchange Online while synchronizing a limited set of those values back to on-premises Active Directory, relevant to hybrid identity environments.

news.title: Advance Zero Trust for AI: New tools and guidance to secure AI agents and DevSecOps
news.summary: Microsoft has expanded its Zero Trust for AI strategy with new tools and guidance targeting AI agents and DevSecOps environments. The release includes specific resources aimed at securing AI workloads within a Zero Trust framework.

news.title: Entra Connect gets a 2026 cutoff as Microsoft urges Tier 0 treatment
news.summary: Microsoft has set a September 30, 2026 deadline for Entra Connect administrators to upgrade to version 2.5.79.0 or later, after which synchronization will stop on older versions. Microsoft is also calling for Entra Connect to be treated as a Tier 0 asset, reflecting its privileged role in hybrid identity infrastructure.

news.title: Obsidian Security raises $85M as AI agents create cybersecurity’s next major attack surface
news.summary: Obsidian Security raised an $85 million Series D funding round, reaching a $1.1 billion post-money valuation. The company focuses on securing access by autonomous AI agents to cloud applications, positioning it within the identity and access management space as AI-driven non-human identities become a growing concern.

news.title: ServiceNow gives Autonomous Security AI Specialists to close exposures faster
news.summary: ServiceNow is launching Autonomous Security AI Specialists, a framework that unifies six security areas including identity governance and vulnerability management. The AI agents are designed to investigate and remediate security issues with limited human intervention.

news.title: Rubrik unveils Agent Identity to govern AI agents one tool call at a time
news.summary: Rubrik unveiled "Agent Identity" at Black Hat, a service designed to govern AI agent access by granting permissions on a per-tool-call basis. The service addresses the emerging challenge of managing and controlling what AI agents are authorized to do within enterprise environments.

news.title: Russian hackers abuse hotel Wi-Fi networks to steal Microsoft 365 credentials and deploy malware
news.summary: Russian threat group Midnight Blizzard has been conducting attacks targeting users on hotel and conference center Wi-Fi networks to steal Microsoft 365 credentials. Microsoft Threat Intelligence identified the campaign, which involves credential theft and malware deployment against M365 users on public networks.

news.title: Azure operations assistant puts incident creation behind a human approval gate
news.summary: Microsoft has introduced an Azure operations assistant that implements a human approval gate for incident creation in agentic IT automation workflows. The system runs read-only diagnostics automatically while requiring explicit confirmation from the authenticated requester before executing write operations like incident creation.

news.title: ClearVector Report Finds 91% of Production Identities Are Non-Human, Exposing Critical Identity Intelligence Gap
news.summary: ClearVector released an Identity Intelligence Report finding that 91% of production identities are non-human, highlighting gaps in traditional identity security models. The report focuses on security blind spots that occur after authentication, pointing to challenges in managing non-human identities in production environments.

news.title: Microsoft links hotel Wi-Fi attacks to Midnight Blizzard and custom malware
news.summary: Microsoft has attributed the CaptiveCrunch campaign to Russia-linked threat actor Midnight Blizzard, linking hotel Wi-Fi attacks to custom malware targeting Microsoft 365 accounts. The operation uses captive-portal hijacking, device-code phishing, and fake Windows authentication flows to compromise M365 credentials and access.

news.title: Hotel Wi-Fi attacks use custom malware to breach Microsoft 365 accounts
news.summary: Microsoft has attributed a global campaign targeting hospitality Wi-Fi networks to Russian threat actor Midnight Blizzard (APT29), which uses custom malware to compromise Microsoft 365 accounts. The attacks involve breaching hotel Wi-Fi networks to intercept credentials and gain unauthorized access to M365 accounts of guests.

news.title: Google Password Manager Attacks Could Let Malware Hijack Passkey-Protected Accounts
news.summary: Unit 42 researchers detailed three attack paths against Google Password Manager's passkey implementation on Windows, collectively called "Pass-ta-key," "Silver Pass-ta-key," and "Golden Pass-ta-key." The most severe attack allows malware running with ordinary user privileges to authenticate to passkey-protected accounts silently, without triggering any visible prompts or requiring biometric input from the victim.

news.title: Migrate2GSA brings a safer Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access migration path
news.summary: An open-source toolkit called Migrate2GSA has been released to simplify migrations to Microsoft Entra Global Secure Access. The tool preserves existing Secure Service Edge configurations, converts them into a reviewable format, and eliminates the need to manually rebuild applications and policies from scratch.

news.title: HubSpot Redesigns JITA Authorization with Rule Engine Architecture
news.summary: HubSpot has redesigned its Just-In-Time Access (JITA) authorization system using a rule engine architecture built on a directed acyclic graph structure. The system evaluates access requests through independent rules with structured decision metadata and rule-level logging, representing a significant architectural approach to dynamic privileged access management.

news.title: Lessons Learned from CISA’s Recent GitHub Leak
news.summary: CISA published a postmortem after a contractor exposed dozens of internal credentials, including AWS GovCloud keys, in a public GitHub repository for nearly six months. The incident highlights credential management failures and gaps in secrets detection practices relevant to IAM and privileged access management teams.

news.title: Scattered Spider Hackers Plead Guilty on Day 1 of Trial
news.summary: Two members of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group pleaded guilty in the UK to charges related to an August 2024 cyberattack on Transport for London. Scattered Spider is known for sophisticated social engineering and identity-based attacks, including SIM swapping and MFA bypass techniques used to compromise organizational systems.
